prompts.text: What does a market reveal about a city that a shopping centre might not?
Tell me about a conversation with a market seller that taught you something about local life.
You're introducing a visitor to an unfamiliar market. What would you want them to notice beyond the products?
Traditional markets often preserve social customs as well as ways of trading.
Walking through an early-morning produce market or exploring the craftspeople working behind small stalls?
The voices, smells and routines of a market can create a sense of place even before you recognise the goods.
Have you ever noticed how bargaining customs differ between places or communities?
A city plans to modernise an old market. What would you ask the existing traders before suggesting changes?
Describe seeing a market prepare for a major festival or seasonal event.
How do regular customers and sellers turn ordinary commerce into a form of community?
What kind of building tells you something about how its community likes to gather?
Tell me about visiting a traditional home and noticing a feature you hadn't seen before.
You can spend a day with someone who restores historic buildings. What design question would you ask?
Architecture reflects practical needs as much as artistic style.
Learning how courtyards shape family life or how traditional roofs respond to local weather?
A building's entrances and shared spaces can influence how often people encounter their neighbours.
Have you noticed designs that look very different but solve the same everyday problem?
Your neighbourhood wants to preserve one old building. How could residents explain its value beyond appearance?
Describe learning why a familiar architectural detail exists instead of assuming it was purely decorative.
How can new architecture respect a community without simply copying historic shapes?
What custom from another place has become part of everyday life where you live?
Tell me about meeting someone whose family history explains an unexpected mixture of traditions.
You're tracing the history of a popular local dish. What routes of migration or trade might you investigate?
Cultural exchange is often visible in small ordinary habits before it appears in formal histories.
Exploring how a musical style crossed borders or following the history of a borrowed word?
A community's culture can change through generations of arrivals without losing its distinctive character.
Have you noticed an expression, ingredient or style that exists in more than one culture under different names?
A family moves to a new country and wants to maintain a meaningful celebration. What parts might be easiest or hardest to preserve?
Describe learning about somebody's home through a tradition they'd adapted after moving away.
How do people create a sense of belonging when they grow up between different cultural backgrounds?
What kind of information can a traditional dance communicate without spoken words?
Tell me about watching a dance performance and discovering that particular movements had a story behind them.
You're learning a community dance where people form a circle. What would you ask about how participants join?
Dance traditions are easier to appreciate when they're seen as ways people relate to one another, not only performances.
Learning the meaning of ceremonial gestures or understanding how social dances have changed with generations?
The arrangement of dancers in a space can reveal something about how people participate together.
Have you noticed how social dances adapt when music or fashion changes?
An archive wants to document a living dance tradition. What should it record beyond the movement itself?
Describe attending a celebration where joining the dance made you feel included in a new community.
How can someone appreciate a dance from another culture without treating it as a costume or novelty?
What kind of joke do people in your community seem to understand without any explanation?
Tell me about humour helping you connect with someone whose everyday experience was different from yours.
A comedian wants to adapt a local joke for an international audience. What might be lost in the translation?
The humour people share can reveal what a community finds familiar, frustrating or worth questioning.
Understanding the history behind a local satire or learning why a familiar expression makes people laugh?
A joke can sound completely ordinary until the listener understands the cultural reference hidden inside it.
Have you ever laughed at a phrase from another language after someone explained the wordplay?
Your friend finds a sketch from decades ago that still feels funny today. What would you want to know about its original audience?
Describe a moment when an unexpected shared sense of humour made a place feel less unfamiliar.
How do communities use humour to discuss subjects that would otherwise be difficult to approach?
What's an everyday object in your community that has a meaning beyond its practical purpose?
Tell me about learning the significance of a small symbol on clothing, pottery or jewellery.
You're curating an exhibit of ordinary objects that carry cultural meaning. What questions would you ask their owners?
A symbol can change meaning between communities even when its appearance stays similar.
Learning about the symbols woven into fabric or understanding the patterns painted on ceremonial objects?
Some designs survive for generations because people recognise the stories they carry.
Have you ever seen a symbol you thought was decorative and discovered it served as a form of communication?
A visitor wants to buy an object associated with a community's sacred or private practice. What would be worth explaining first?
Describe an object whose cultural significance became clearer after hearing the maker's explanation.
How can designers use historical symbols responsibly without assuming they mean the same thing everywhere?
What's a traditional game or sport that reveals something interesting about where people grew up?
Tell me about attending a local sporting event where the surrounding rituals surprised you.
You want to introduce a neighbourhood game to children from several backgrounds. How would you explain its rules and origins?
Community games can preserve local history even when people mainly participate for fun.
Learning how a traditional wrestling event is organised or exploring the history of a community board game?
Sports gatherings can become cultural landmarks through the songs, food and shared routines around them.
Have you noticed different communities celebrating the same sport in distinctive ways?
A local competition wants to preserve its traditional opening ceremony while welcoming new participants. What could help?
Describe a game you played as a child that people from another area knew by a different name.
What would you ask someone who has helped organise a local sporting tradition for decades?
What's a mural, sculpture or public artwork that made you curious about the people who created it?
Tell me about discovering the story behind a piece of art you used to pass without noticing.
Your neighbourhood commissions a mural about its history. How would you make sure residents' different stories are heard?
Public art can make cultural memory visible even when a community has no formal museum.
A temporary street-art festival or a permanent artwork built with contributions from local craftspeople?
An artwork in a public place changes as the surrounding neighbourhood changes.
How does the meaning of a public monument shift when a new generation begins asking questions about it?
A visitor misinterprets a symbol on a local mural. What information would help them understand the artist's intention?
Describe a public artwork that sparked an interesting conversation among people seeing it together.
Who should decide what stories are represented in shared public spaces?
What kind of ordinary photograph can reveal more about a community than a formal portrait?
Tell me about seeing an old image of a familiar place and noticing how daily life had changed.
You can photograph one typical day in a neighbourhood without staging anything. What moments would you try to capture?
A photograph can document a culture while still showing only one person's point of view.
A collection of candid images from a market or a series of portraits with people's own stories alongside them?
The details in the background of an old photograph often become the most valuable historical clues.
How can photographers represent people respectfully when documenting traditions outside their own communities?
An archive receives photographs with no captions. What would you want to learn before identifying their subjects?
Describe discovering that a family photograph was connected to a wider historical event.
What everyday aspect of life today would you want future generations to see in photographs?
What everyday word in your language originally came from somewhere else?
Tell me about recognising a familiar-sounding word in a language you hadn't studied.
You're tracing how a borrowed word entered local speech. Who would you ask about its older uses?
Borrowed words can preserve a history of contact that people no longer think about consciously.
Comparing how neighbouring languages name foods or exploring how local accents develop around shared words?
New expressions often spread through friendship groups before anybody writes them down.
Have you noticed younger and older speakers choosing different words for the same modern object?
A community wants to document phrases used by elders that children rarely hear. How could younger people participate?
Describe discovering that one local phrase had several meanings depending on who said it.
How do languages remain recognisable while constantly adopting new words and expressions?
